title: Afghanistan to Host India for T20I Series in Delhi This September
excerpt: Afghanistan will play the designated home side when they face India in three T20Is at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 13, 15, and 17, with FanCode streaming all matches digitally.
body:
• Afghanistan will host India for three T20Is on September 13, 15, and 17 at Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium, with Afghanistan designated as the home team despite the matches being played on Indian soil.
  • FanCode has secured exclusive digital streaming rights, with distribution across eight partner platforms including Jio TV, Amazon Prime, and Tata Play Binge.
  • India enter the series on the back of a difficult T20I stretch, having lost 4-0 to England and 2-0 to Ireland in away series earlier this year.
  • The series is sandwiched between India's Test tour of Sri Lanka and the Asian Games in Japan, making squad selection and workload management key storylines.

Afghanistan will host India for a three-match T20I series at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on September 13, 15, and 17, with the Afghanistan Cricket Board designating the matches as home fixtures despite being played on Indian soil. It marks the first time a team will host India in India — a peculiar arrangement born of Afghanistan's inability to stage international cricket at home since the Taliban takeover in 2021.

A Home Series in Exile

Afghanistan have played their home matches in India for several years, using venues in Lucknow, Dehradun, and Greater Noida, but never against India. The September fixtures will be a first in that regard.

"We have hosted our home fixtures in both India and the UAE in recent years, and given the importance and scale of this series, we believe India provides an excellent setting for the event," Afghanistan Cricket Board Chairman Mirwais Ashraf said in a statement.

"We are committed to supporting the growth of cricket in Afghanistan. We believe there is scope to do more together and will continue to support Afghanistan cricket while strengthening the relationship between the two cricketing nations."

— Mithun Manhas, BCCI President

FanCode Secures Streaming Rights

FanCode has locked in the exclusive digital streaming rights for the series, adding another marquee India property to its expanding cricket portfolio. The platform will distribute matches across mobile, web, and connected TV, with additional reach through eight partner platforms: Jio TV, Amazon Prime, Crex, Jagran, Playbox, Watcho, Tata Play Binge, and Times Prime.

The deal extends FanCode's relationship with the Afghanistan Cricket Board, following its recent coverage of India's tour of Zimbabwe. FanCode also holds partnerships with Cricket West Indies, the ICC, Zimbabwe Cricket, and Cricket Ireland.

India's T20I Form Under Scrutiny

Despite being the reigning T20 World Cup champions, India's recent white-ball results have been poor. A 4-0 T20I series loss in England and a 2-0 defeat in Ireland have raised questions about the team's depth and approach in the shortest format. India are currently in Zimbabwe for a three-match series, looking to stabilize before the bigger challenges ahead.

The September T20Is against Afghanistan are strategically positioned in India's calendar — arriving after the second Test against Sri Lanka ends on August 27 and before the Asian Games begin on September 24 in Japan. The scheduling creates a tight window that could influence squad selection, with selectors likely balancing workload management against the need to rebuild T20I confidence.

Afghanistan's Resurgence

Afghanistan have not played a T20I since the T20 World Cup earlier this year, where they won two of their four group-stage matches but narrowly missed a Super Eight spot. Their ODI form has been strong, however, with recent series wins over Ireland.

India's recent record against Afghanistan is dominant — an innings-and-300-run win in a one-off Test and a 3-0 ODI sweep when the sides last met in June. In T20Is, India have won all three previous meetings. But Afghanistan's unpredictable spin attack, led by Rashid Khan, remains a threat capable of disrupting any batting lineup on a given day.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For the Indian diaspora, the series represents accessible cricket content during a period typically dominated by football and the tail end of European league seasons. FanCode's wide distribution network ensures fans across platforms can follow the action live. The scheduling — 7:00 PM IST starts (6:30 AM Pacific, 9:30 AM Eastern) — falls within workable viewing windows for NRI audiences in North America, though early risers on the West Coast will have the best seats.

With the ODI World Cup 2027 on the horizon, this series also offers a preview of the emerging talent pipeline both boards are building. The real question for India: can they arrest a T20I slide before confidence becomes a deeper problem?
